verdict.why: From the lens of evidence, sources, and measurability, Option Y is significantly more buildable, explicit, and faithful to the brief's task list. (1) Task 1 in the brief requires a 'review where the spec loop, the consilium script, research and other stages call which model and on which route'; Option Y explicitly delivers this in 'Design 1. Review of call sites' (a 12-row table mapping Today vs. Target) and includes a measurable grep verification step (row 12 and T16), whereas Option X omits the current-state review entirely. (2) For measurability of the thinker-to-writer split, Option Y defines a strict JSON schema (`Contracts C3`, `meanings-<N>.json`), exact system prompt text (`Contracts C2`), and verifiable inline `[M<n>]` citation tags checked via regex (`Design 3`, `T6`, `T7`), plus a `gaps.md` hash check. Option X relies on a looser Markdown meanings file and leaves 14 tactical/unknown questions (`Q4`–`Q17`) marked `by: pending` in its Questions table, whereas Option Y resolves all tactical questions (`by: agent`) and leaves only 3 genuine strategy questions (`Q1`–`Q3`) with defaults. (3) For spend accounting and cost evidence, Option Y specifies an exact 5-step cost extraction algorithm (`Design 5`, `spend.cost_from_usage`), handles OpenRouter activity tracking (`X-Title` and `user` payload fields), prevents double-counting between local spend and lagging provider figures via `max(observatory_usd, local_month_usd)` (`Design 6`), and includes a concrete fixture-capture step (`Rollout step 2`). (4) For quality preservation (Brief item 4), Option Y defines a measurable canary protocol (`REQ-14`, `Rollout step 6`) comparing round-1 accepted blocker/major findings against a 3-spec baseline, and passes `--meanings` to the judge (`Design 4`, `T12`) so the judge can empirically verify whether the writer dropped any meanings. (5) For the word-count ratchet, Option Y provides the exact replacement Markdown text and line-by-line diffs (`Design 7`), making compliance immediately verifiable before implementation.
risks: Option Y's decision to require a paid thinker call for Size S specs (Decisions, Q5) when the split is in force could incur unnecessary token spend on trivial tasks, though it strictly follows the owner's order which gave no size exemption.

Option Y's strict 'no retry on any failure' rule for validators (REQ-4, Design 4) means transient network/HTTP 500 errors will drop panelists and could cause a 5-member panel to fall below the 3-verdict minimum more often than Option X's unbilled-retry rule (D11).

Passing `--meanings` to the Fable judge (Option Y, Design 4) ensures text-to-meaning fidelity is measured, but increases the risk of confirmation bias since Fable authored the meanings; however, the blind 5-vendor panel and baseline canary metric (Rollout step 6) mitigate this.
